_meta.coverage_metric: universal Constraint-First entry topology, A/B/C/D complexity classification, anti-degradation, source-claim separation, domain decoupling, exact-subject binding, realm/boundary/flow closure, state and invariant references, required-capability gating, teardown symmetry, performance measurement closure, evidence-state separation, and repeated-failure recovery routing
_meta.purpose: Prove that an incomplete software prompt or architecture cannot skip constraint discovery into plausible implementation, that Level C/D work cannot silently degrade into Level A behavior, that domain modules extend rather than replace the universal compiler, and that structurally hollow system contracts or repeated blind repairs are refused.

runnable.hollow_fixture: remove the Level C/D anti-degradation law or allow a domain module to replace/bypass the universal constraint compiler
covers: the entrypoint is a pre-implementation constraint discovery compiler rather than a substrate-only implementation recipe
the canonical topology is Universal System Prompt to source intent to Constraint Compiler to domain/unknown/hard-law expansion to Executable Spec to Implementation to Harness/Evals
Level A/B/C/D complexity classes are explicit
Level C/D work cannot silently degrade into Level A implementation behavior
the universal transformation is intent to boundary to state to invariant to failure to oracle to evidence to implementation
required pre-implementation output includes Intent Digest through Implementation Gate before Implementation Plan
domain modules extend the core method and may not replace or bypass it
runnable.expected: canonical universal entry admitted; planted anti-degradation and domain-replacement regressions are distinguishable

runnable.hollow_fixture: runtime mutations that remove an invariant oracle or teardown ledger, advance an unexercised capability to READY_FOR_IMPLEMENTATION, add a vague low-latency claim, make PASS evidence-free, or introduce dangling state/transition references
covers: the exact subject has a revision and lowercase SHA-256 digest
realms, boundaries, flows, states, resources, and teardown references close
every hard invariant has an enforcement owner, executable or planned oracle, and named failure state
required capability and assumption states gate READY_FOR_IMPLEMENTATION
every lifecycle-owned resource has normal and crash teardown plus a leak oracle
performance claims require metric, target, percentile, load model, environment identity, measurement method, and repetitions
PASS and FAIL require evidence while absence and non-execution remain distinct
a missing contract file is an input error rather than a failed system
runnable.expected: canonical prototype contract admitted; each planted hollow or contradictory mutation refused with a stable reason

runnable.hollow_fixture: removing the qualifying-failure definition, allowing a fourth blind patch, removing Forgejo/GitHub routing, reusing the stale diagnosis context, removing the isolated-worktree requirement, allowing commit before the owning oracle passes, or silently granting merge authority
covers: three consecutive qualifying failures against the same invariant or acceptance target force escalation rather than a fourth blind patch
the issue packet preserves exact subject, oracle, three failure trajectories, falsified hypotheses, unknowns, and rollback context
normal repositories with an admitted local Forgejo binding route issue and PR work through Forgejo
GitHub Actions and GitHub-hosted CI incidents remain on GitHub with exact workflow/run/job/head evidence
fresh diagnosis uses a new context and ChatGPT Desktop is a host/operator handoff when the runtime cannot launch it
the repair starts in a new isolated worktree/branch with one writer
commit and PR eligibility require the owning oracle and required negative control to pass
merge to main remains governed by the repository's existing Human or separately admitted trusted-operator policy
runnable.expected: recovery contract contains all mandatory stop, routing, fresh-context, worktree, verification, publication, and merge-authority boundaries
